hook.line: This is an AI supercomputer with two terabytes of RAM.
hook.visual: Blurred face close-up, then he lifts a stack of four silver Mac Studios to the lens; a glowing '2TB RAM' title appears over the stack at 2.25 s.

beats.what: Face rushes into frame, then he hoists the four-machine stack toward camera
Zoom punch onto the stack with '2TB RAM' glowing above it
He dares the viewer: 'go ahead, name one'
Top-half card: DeepSeek logo, 'V3.1 671b' and a gold check, face below
Kimi K2 trillion-parameter claim in green word-highlight captions
Terminal UI of model instances loading across the four machines
Close-up of his finger tapping the stack: 'still not sweating'
Terminal with a hand-drawn yellow arrow on the tokens-per-second number
macOS Software Update screenshot introduces the RDMA feature, then he withholds the answer
Old CRT television cutaway as he points to 'the link right here'

characters.who: The stack of four Mac Studios (hero prop)
characters.enters: Lifted up into the lens by both hands at 0.38 s
characters.acts: Lit with a glowing title, tapped, patted and kept beside him on the desk as the proof object
characters.exits: Never leaves; it stays on the desk at frame edge

why_it_works: A physical hero object lifted to the lens in the first second gives a concrete thing to stare at before any explanation
Call-and-response with the viewer ('name one', 'both at the same time?') escalates the stakes every few seconds
Cuts every 1.76 s (median) plus two zoom punches keep the eye moving
Curiosity gap at the end: he names RDMA but refuses to explain it, pushing viewers to the long video
weaknesses: The withheld payoff can feel like bait to viewers who never click through
Caption position jumps between top, middle and bottom
for_robert: Treat one object as a co-star: lift it to the lens in the first second and keep it on the desk all video; Fred could be that object, held up at the hook and reacting to each claim.
